The rebase that replays a squash

The commit rule told you to run git rebase main after the parent landed. In a repo that squash merges, that is the one command guaranteed to conflict.

Walk the stack


    

  


  

    
What the rule says now

    
TRUNK=$(git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD | sed 's|^origin/||')
OLD_PARENT=$(git rev-parse origin/feature/auth-base)   # BEFORE the parent merges
OLD_TIP=$(git rev-parse origin/feature/auth-service)   # the lease

git rebase --onto "origin/$TRUNK" "$OLD_PARENT" feature/auth-service
git push --force-with-lease=feature/auth-service:"$OLD_TIP" origin feature/auth-service

    
A bare --force-with-lease checks the local
      remote tracking ref, which a background fetch can update behind you. Naming the branch and
      the sha is what makes the check mean anything.

  


  

    
Four traps, folded into the reference

    
1. auto-merge      refused on a native stack layer, land via the stack merge API
2. submit --auto   opens every layer as a DRAFT, and a stack with a draft cannot merge
                   use --auto --open
3. stack init      reads the LOCAL origin/HEAD, which goes stale
                   pass it: gh stack init -b "$TRUNK"
4. the event       parent merges, and about 2s later the layer above gets
                   automatic_base_change_succeeded + head_ref_force_pushed
                   together, as a pair, and never `edited`
                   do not key on edited, and do not wait for a second event

  


  

    Also in this PR: create-pr gained the stacked path its own eval case has been
    asking for since the case was written, and the case gained a fifth expectation covering the
    recorded parent tip.
